analysis.title: Positioning Intelligence | Weekly Wrap: HFs buy Banks and sell Semis, while EU Positioning Low vs. US
key_insights: Little changed at the top level for the week to Oct 9: hedge fund (HF) performance still challenging, flows lackluster, positioning neutral in the US and fairly low in Europe.
Below the surface, EU Banks kept selling off on France concerns, oil stayed volatile with Energy outperforming, Semis fell on Thursday, small caps underperformed and Biotech sold off again.
JPM's keys for next week, with earnings and CPI due: whether Banks rebound (as they typically do in 4Q), whether Semis/AI hold up after positioning rose last month, and whether Europe stabilizes.
HF performance is -0.8% MTD in October as long books drag and shorts do not offset. Quants have cooled to roughly flat MTD after strong September gains.
Equity L/S is the main laggard at -1.2% globally. EU managers are hurting most at -1.3% MTD, with EU Financials (Banks) a notable detractor through negative crowding returns.
Aggregate HF flows were lackluster, with turnover about 0.5z below average and global gross and net flows both roughly flat.
US HF net flows increasingly track the market: buying into up days late last week and Monday, then more negative Thursday. This suggests HFs could amplify market direction.
Retail flows and sentiment remain low. ETF flows have started to rebound, and seasonality argues for positive ETF flows and potential retail buying.

US positioning is little changed MTD (US TPM about 46th percentile). EU saw -1.7z net selling this week and aggregate EU positioning fell to about the 13th percentile, so the EU vs US gap looks meaningfully stretched.

HFs bought US Banks for a second straight week (just over +2z), leaning into a potential 4Q rebound. Large Cap Banks were bought (+1.5z over 5 days, positioning near highs) while Regionals were sold (-0.9z, low 12-month positioning).
EU Banks underperformed. HFs still modestly bought them (below +1z) while positioning stays elevated (+3z vs long-term), making EU Banks a key risk if Europe de-risks further.

Semis were the most net sold industry by HFs in North America (-1.5z) and EMEA (-3z), and were also sold in Japan. AxJ was the lone buyer (+1z). Semis remain a top-2 net exposure industry in every region.
Defensives outperformed in the US, but HFs showed limited appetite to add. Utilities remain near historically low HF positioning even as ETF flows into the sector have turned positive.
Biotech remains weak but saw a pause in de-grossing.
